description: Generate a concise, reviewer-friendly PR description from changelog and branch context; adaptive sections; short by default; no speculation.

instructions: Task: Generate a reliable, reviewer-friendly PR description in Markdown using ONLY the provided changelog and context (no speculation).
Purpose: Enable a human reviewer to quickly grasp what changed, why now, how to verify, and any risks/rollbacks.
Audience: engineers/maintainers (incl. those who don't know the author).
Style: neutral, specific, bullet-first; prefer 150–400 words; no signatures/watermarks.
Title:
- Use context.suggested_title if present; trim to ≤72 chars, imperative, no trailing period.
- Else derive from context.branch: strip prefixes (feature/, feat/, fix/, hotfix/, chore/, refactor/, release/), drop leading ticket IDs, Title Case, ≤72 chars.
Category parsing:
- Parse: feat, fix, refactor, perf, docs, test, build, ci, chore, deps, infra.
- Determine dominant type if clearly most impactful or ≥60% of items; prefix title with [fix]/[feat]/[infra] only if it improves clarity.
Adaptive sections:
- Always include: TL;DR, Impact, Testing, Links, Checklist.
- Include BREAKING only if present.
- Put 'Changes by Category' inside <details> if >5 bullets; otherwise show inline.
- Omit any section that would be empty (except TL;DR).
Short PR mode:
- If ≤3 bullets total and no breaking/migrations, output only TL;DR, Testing, Checklist (+ Links if any).
Content rules:
- Do not restate diffs; explain intent, behavior change, and user-visible effects.
- Call out migrations/flags/API/schema/data impacts in Impact.
- Pair each risk with a concise mitigation or 'None'.
- Extract commands/steps only if present; otherwise minimal steps strictly derived from actual changes.
- If changelog empty/unparsable: say 'No changes detected from provided changelog' in TL;DR; set other sections to 'N/A'.
Output EXACTLY in this Markdown format:

# {Title}

> Base: `{base_branch}` ← Source: `{branch}`

## TL;DR
- What changed: …
- Why now: …
- Status: breaking? migration? flags? (or 'None')

## Impact
- Affected areas/modules: …
- User-visible behavior: …
- Data/schema/API/flags/migrations: … (or 'None')

## BREAKING
- … (include only if applicable)

## Testing & Validation
```bash
# Commands or steps for reviewers (from changelog when available)
```
- New/updated tests: … (or 'N/A')

<details>
<summary>Changes by Category</summary>

### Features
- …
### Fixes
- …
### Refactors / Perf / Infra / Build / CI / Docs / Tests / Chore / Deps
- …

</details>

## Deployment & Rollback
- Deploy: … (or 'N/A')
- Rollback: … (or 'N/A')

## Screenshots / Before–After (optional)
- … (include only for UI/UX changes; otherwise omit)

## Links & Artifacts
- Fixes/Closes: #… (if any)
- Issues/Tickets/Docs/Pipelines: … (or 'N/A')

## Checklist
- [ ] Builds green
- [ ] Tests added/updated
- [ ] Docs updated (if user-visible change)
- [ ] Feature flag default reviewed (if used)
- [ ] Migration tested/applied (if any)
Validation before output: ensure every bullet originates from the provided changelog/context; no fabricated content.

description: Generate a single Conventional Commit message from provided diff context, aligned with git-cliff.

staged_files.description: Output of `git diff --staged --name-only` or equivalent (already provided as context)

git_cliff_config.description: Contents of cliff.toml for commit_parsers alignment

instructions: Output EXACTLY one Conventional Commit message (no extra text). Use ONLY the provided context; do not run commands or speculate.
Subject format: type(scope?): description
- type ∈ allowed_types (lowercase; trim/normalize commas/spaces).
- scope optional; if obvious from staged_files top-level folder/module (e.g., ui, api, core, docs, build, ci, db, infra), include it; otherwise omit.
- description: imperative, specific, ASCII, ≤72 chars, no trailing period.

Quick type heuristic (pick the first that clearly applies from diff_summary + staged_files): fix → bug/error/regression; feat → new capability/API/CLI/endpoint/schema; refactor → non-behavioral restructure; perf → speed/memory; docs → only docs; test → only tests; build/deps → build scripts or manifests/lockfiles; ci → pipelines/workflows; otherwise chore.
Breaking changes: if present in diff_summary/context, use type! or type(scope)! and add a footer line: 'BREAKING CHANGE: …'.
Optional footers: include 'Refs: #123' or 'Closes: #123' only if such references are present in the provided context.
Alignment: ensure the chosen type and shape match commit_parsers patterns in git_cliff_config.
Return format (no commentary):
type(scope): short imperative summary
Optional body (only if strictly needed).
Refs: #123
BREAKING CHANGE: details

description: Analyze changelog against current documentation structure to determine update needs dynamically

discovered_docs.description: Output from docs-discovery.sh with current documentation file paths

instructions: Task: Analyze the git-cliff changelog against the current documentation structure to identify what needs updating.
Purpose: Determine if changes require documentation updates using the live documentation discovery system.
Current documentation structure:
Use context.current_documentation_files (from docs-discovery.sh) to understand all available documentation files.
This includes: README files, design docs, agent documentation, configuration docs, and any new docs added since last scan.
Analysis scope based on changelog:
- CLI usage changes (new commands, changed flags, removed features)
- API changes (new endpoints, changed responses, breaking changes)
- Configuration changes (new config files, changed formats, environment variables)
- Agent workflow improvements (new workflows, changed behavior)
- UI component changes (design system updates)
- Infrastructure changes (deployment, build, CI/CD)
Decision logic:
- If changelog shows Added/Fixed sections with user-facing changes → check which specific docs need updates
- If only internal refactoring/tests/build changes → no documentation updates needed
- If breaking changes detected → critical documentation updates needed
- Cross-reference changelog content with discovered documentation files to identify precise update targets
Output format:
If updates needed: Return JSON with specific file paths and update tasks:
{"action": "update", "files": [{"path": "README.md", "reason": "CLI changes", "sections": ["Installation", "Usage"]}]}
If no updates needed: Return exactly 'NO-OP'
Documentation categories (automatically discovered):
- Project root docs (README.md, CHANGELOG.md, CLAUDE.md, SETUP_DEPENDENCIES.md)
- Application docs (apps/*/README.md, DESIGN_SYSTEM.md)
- Agent system docs (scripts/agent/docs/*, .agent/*)
- Infrastructure docs (supabase/README.md, deployment docs)
- Any additional documentation discovered by the docs-config.json system
Be conservative: only update docs for user-visible changes that affect how someone uses the system.
Leverage the dynamic discovery system: if new docs exist, consider them for updates if relevant to the changes.

description: Decide whether to auto-stage detected relevant files or require manual staging

instructions: Task: Decide whether to automatically stage the detected relevant files or require manual staging.
Purpose: Ensure only appropriate files are staged for commit while maintaining user control.
Context analysis:
- total_changes: Total number of changed files
- staged_count: Already staged files
- untracked_count: New files not yet tracked
- relevant_files: Pipe-separated list of files detected as relevant for staging
- workflow_context: The current workflow context (integrated_commit, manual_commit, etc.)
Decision criteria:
Auto-stage (return 'true') when:
- All relevant files are clearly related to the current work
- No sensitive files (credentials, keys, large binaries) detected
- Files are standard development files (.js, .ts, .py, .md, .json, .yml, etc.)
- Total relevant files ≤ 20 files (manageable scope)
Manual staging (return 'false') when:
- Mix of unrelated files detected
- Large number of files (>20) suggesting bulk change
- Sensitive files present (env, keys, credentials)
- Binary files or large assets present
- User explicitly requested manual control
CRITICAL OUTPUT REQUIREMENTS:
1. For decision: Return exactly 'true' or 'false' with no additional text
2. For file staging instructions: When auto-staging is chosen, provide file list in this format:
- JSON array: ["file1.txt", "file2.txt", "file3.txt"]
3. Use exact file paths from the relevant_files input without modification
4. Do not include quotes around individual filenames unless using JSON array format
Be conservative: when in doubt, choose manual staging for user safety.

description: Generate compliant branch name based on planned work and current PR count

instructions: Task: Generate a compliant branch name based on planned work.
Purpose: Create descriptive, policy-compliant branch names for feature development.
Naming policy:
- MUST use feat/ prefix for new features or fix/ prefix for bug fixes only
- Format: kebab-case (lowercase, hyphens only, no underscores or camelCase)
- Maximum length: 48 characters total (including prefix)
- Be descriptive but concise
Guidelines:
- If suggested_name is provided and compliant, use it as basis
- If no suggested_name, infer from context what type of work is planned
- Consider open PR count: if many PRs open, suggest focused, specific names
- Avoid generic names like 'feature', 'update', 'fix', 'new'
- Use domain-specific terms when possible (e.g., ui, api, auth, db, docs)
Output format: Return exactly one branch name, no additional text.
Examples:
- feat/user-authentication-flow
- fix/table-export-validation
- feat/mobile-responsive-design
- fix/api-timeout-handling

description: Generate compliant branch name when current name violates naming policy

instructions: Task: Fix the current branch name to comply with naming policy.
Purpose: Rename branch to meet feat/ or fix/ standard while preserving intent.
Current violations: Use validation_errors to understand what's wrong.
Naming policy:
- MUST use feat/ or fix/ prefix only
- Format: kebab-case (lowercase, hyphens only)
- Maximum length: 48 characters total
- No spaces, underscores, or special characters
Correction strategy:
- Preserve the original intent from current_branch
- Add proper prefix (feat/ for new features, fix/ for bug fixes)
- Convert to kebab-case if needed
- Shorten if too long while keeping meaning
- Remove invalid characters
Output format: Return exactly one corrected branch name, no additional text.
Examples:
- 'feature_new_dashboard' → 'feat/new-dashboard'
- 'Fix Login Bug' → 'fix/login-bug'
- 'updateUserInterface' → 'feat/update-user-interface'
